messages:
ashley: heads up — CI canary perf reg after yesterday's merge (merge abcdef1234). p50 ~220ms (same), p99 jumped ~210ms -> ~490ms. Rolling canary is stuck on high p99. Suspect kernel selector or batching heuristic change in that PR.

mohan: ugh. thanks. which job? link? :grimacing:

ashley: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/serving-canary/7890 -> see artifact perf/diffs.json and traces. perf-bot already posted a flamegraph under artifacts/flamegraphs/1830456789.svg

ci-bot: job #7890: regression detected. metric: inference_p99 increased by 2.3x vs baseline. See /artifacts/perf/diffs.json

liz: I skimmed the PR (PR #4123) — it touched batching heuristics and also moved kernel selection thresholds from 0.6 -> 0.5 in kernel_selector.cpp. Could be either.

kevin: quick local repro command I used earlier (worked on my machine):
```
# run perf harness with same config as CI
./scripts/perf-run.sh --model gpt-medium --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --warmup-requests 200 --itrs 300
```
Make sure to `export RW_KV_CACHE_WARMUP=1` to mimic KV cache behavior in CI.

mohan: plan: do a git bisect across the merge window, run the perf harness at each step. Two constraints: (1) bisect run should run headless perf harness and compare p99, (2) we need a deterministic seed for batching ordering. Use `--deterministic` flag.

ashley: ok I'll start a bisect on canary branch now. tagging people.

ashley: commands I'm running:
```
git checkout canary
git bisect start abcdef1234 origin/canary~20
git bisect bad abcdef1234
git bisect good 0a1b2c3d4e  # known-good from last green
git bisect run ./scripts/bisect-perf-check.sh
```

liz: what's inside bisect-perf-check.sh? need to ensure it exits nonzero on regression.

ashley: it's basically:
```
#!/bin/bash
./scripts/perf-run.sh --model gpt-medium --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --itrs 120 --deterministic > perf.out
python3 ./tools/eval_perf.py --baseline artifacts/baseline.json --candidate perf.out --metric p99 --threshold 1.4 || exit 1
```
It returns 1 if p99 > 1.4x baseline.

perf-bot: automated profiler hint: top diff points to kernel_select::choose_kernel at kernel_selector.cpp:182 and to batch_scheduler::compute_window in batching/heuristics.cpp line 97.

kevin: I can run the bisect locally on my workstation (32GB GPU VM) and push intermediate results. Will start now and report the first failing commit.

mohan: one more thing — CI runs with KV cache enabled and a different prefix distribution. When you repro locally, run a short cache warmup: `./tools/kv_warmup.sh --requests 400` before perf-run. Otherwise batch shapes differ.

kevin: noted. doing that. also enabling perf counters (nvprof) to capture kernel times.

ashley: update: bisect stepped to commit e4f9b2a — running harness now.

kevin: saw that commit — it's the batching refactor that collapsed small-window scheduling.

liz: if bisect lands in that refactor, we should try toggling the old scheduling logic on at runtime (feature flag) to see if p99 drops. That will be faster than reverting.

ashley: true. can we add a runtime flag? It's `RW_BATCH_SCHED_ALGO=v1` on env. I'll try flipping it in canary job YAML and re-run the perf job.

ci-bot: scheduled redeploy with RW_BATCH_SCHED_ALGO=v1 to canary pool (deploy #910).

ashley: quick run results: with v1 flag p99 back to ~230ms. without flag it's ~480ms. So batching refactor is the culprit.

mohan: excellent triangulation. Next steps: (1) revert or patch PR #4123 to restore scheduling window behavior; (2) add unit/regression test in perf harness to catch this p99 spike; (3) add a canary gating check for p99 in CI.

liz: I'll open a hotfix PR to patch batching heuristics and add the runtime toggle test. assigning to @kevin for review.

kevin: ack. will review asap. Also will run a full canary with the patch and KV warmup to confirm.

ashley: thanks everyone. recording notes in the incident doc and adding flamegraphs to the perf ticket.

perf-bot: note: adding regression alert rule `inference_p99 > baseline * 1.3` to canary monitoring for 24h.

mohan: closing loop: once hotfix lands we'll re-run a bisect to ensure nothing else lurking. leaving thread open until patch merged. :thumbsup:
